content:
iOS 27 comes packed with powerful features like Siri AI and upgrades to productivity apps including Apple Mail, Notes, Reminders, and Calendar. But for many users, the best changes in iOS 27 may be some bug fixes that make apps run more smoothly — here are three fixes coming to Apple Mail.

Apple Mail in iOS 27 has improved badge accuracy, faster message loading, and more reliable search.

While iOS 27 is loaded with new features, Apple also took extra time to make this update run smoother and more stable than ever.

Although Apple rarely makes bug fixes a selling point, that's exactly what happened when iOS 27 was announced.

Among the many usability improvements in iOS 27, three Apple Mail fixes should benefit long-time users:

  • Improved unread badge accuracy
  • Faster message loading
  • More reliable search indexing

These three improvements were highlighted on a massive slide containing hundreds of small and large changes in iOS 27.

The unread badge accuracy issue has been my personal pet peeve for years. I have badges turned off for most of my apps, but among the few that still have them on, Mail is the most problematic, with phantom badges or inaccurate counts appearing frequently.

Messages in the inbox taking forever to open is equally frustrating, but Apple has sped up message loading in iOS 27.

OK

Just one simple change would bring me back to Apple Mail: treat attachments as attachments instead of turning them into inline content.

Results may vary, but I've found the search improvements in iOS 27 Mail to be quite noticeable.

Beyond these bug fixes, iOS 27 also adds several new features to Apple Mail. So if you haven't used Mail in a while, iOS 27 might be a good time to give it another try.

How is your Apple Mail performing in the iOS 27 beta? Feel free to share in the comments.
